title: Largest eigenvalue and top eigenvector statistics of large Euclidean random matrices
summary: Euclidean random matrices arise in a wide range of physical systems where interactions are determined by spatial configurations, including disordered media and cooperative phenomena in atomic ensembles. Unlike classical random matrix ensembles, their entries are strongly correlated through the geometry of the underlying random points, making their analytical treatment challenging.
